source.text: Μετὰ δὲ δέκα καὶ πέντε ἡμέρας νηστεύσαντός μου καὶ πολλὰ ἐρωτήσαντος τὸν Κύριον ἀπεκαλύφθη μοι ἡ γνῶσις τῆς γραφῆς. ἦν δὲ γεγραμμένα ταῦτα· 2. Τὸ σπέρμα σου, Ἑρμᾶ, ἠθέτησαν εἰς τὸν Θεὸν καὶ ἐβλασφήμησαν εἰς τὸν Κύριον καὶ προέδωκαν τοὺς γονεῖς αὐτῶν ἐν πονηρίᾳ μεγάλῃ, καὶ ἤκουσαν προδότας γονέων, καὶ προδόντες οὐκ ὠφελήθησαν, ἀλλὰ ἔτι προσεθήκαν ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις αὐτῶν τὰς ἀσελγηίας καὶ συμφυρμοὺς πονηρίας, καὶ οὕτως ἐπλήσθησαν αἱ ἀνομίαι αὐτῶν. 3. ἀλλὰ γνώρισον ταῦτα τὰ ῥήματα τοῖς τέκνοις σου πᾶσιν καὶ τῇ συμβίῳ σου τῇ μελλούσῃ σου ἀδελφῇ· καὶ γὰρ αὕτη οὐκ ἀπέχεται τῆς γλώσσης, ἐν ᾗ πονηρεύεται· ἀλλὰ ἀκούσασα τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα ἀφέξεται, καὶ ἕξει ἔλεος. 4. μετὰ τὸ γνωρίσαι σε ταῦτα τὰ ῥήματα αὐτοῖς ἃ ἐνετείλατό μοι ὁ δεσπότης ἵνα σοι ἀποκαλυφθῇ, τότε ἀφίενται αὐτοῖς αἱ ἁμαρτίαι πᾶσαι ἃς πρότερον ἥμαρτον, καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ἁγίοις τοῖς ἁμαρτήσασιν μέχρι ταύτης τῆς ἡμέρας, ἐὰν ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας μετανοήσωσιν καὶ ἄρωσιν ἀπὸ τῆς καρδίας αὐτῶν τὰς διψυχίας. 5. ὤμοσεν γὰρ ὁ δεσπότης κατὰ τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τοὺς ἐκλεκτοὺς αὐτοῦ· ἐὰν ὡρισμένης τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης ἔτι ἁμάρτησις γένηται, μὴ ἔχειν αὐτοὺς σωτηρίαν· ἡ γὰρ μετάνοια τοῖς δικαίοις ἔχει τέλος· πεπλήρωνται αἱ ἡμέραι μετανοίας πᾶσιν τοῖς ἁγίοις· καὶ τοῖς δὲ ἔθνεσιν μετάνοιά ἐστιν ἕως ἐσχάτης ἡμέρας. 6. ἐρεῖς οὖν τοῖς προηγουμένοις τῆς ἐκκλησίας ἵνα κατορθώσωνται τὰς ὁδοὺς αὐτῶν ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ, ἵνα ἀπολάβωσιν ἐκ πλήρους τὰς ἐπαγγελίας μετὰ πολλῆς δόξης. 7. ἐμμείνατε οὖν οἱ ἐργαζόμενοι τὴν δικαιοσύνην καὶ μὴ διψυχήσητε, ἵνα γένηται ὑμῶν ἡ πάροδος μετὰ τῶν ἀγγέλων τῶν ἁγίων. μακάριοι ὑμεῖς ὅσοι ὑπομένετε τὴν θλῖψιν τὴν ἐρχομένην τὴν μεγάλην, καὶ ὅσοι οὐκ ἀρνήσονται τὴν ζωὴν αὐτῶν. 8. ὤμοσεν γὰρ Κύριος κατὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, τοὺς ἀρνησαμένους τὸν Κύριον αὐτῶν ἀπεγνωσθαι ἀπὸ τῆς ζωῆς αὐτῶν, τοὺς νῦν μέλλοντας ἀρνεῖσθαι ταῖς ἐρχομέναις ἡμέραις· τοῖς δὲ πρότερον ἀρνησαμένοις διὰ τὴν πολυσπλαγχνίαν ἵλεως ἐγένετο αὐτοῖς.

translation.text:
After fifteen days[1], when I had been fasting and had asked the Lord many things, the understanding of the writing was revealed to me.[1] And this was written:

“Your offspring, Hermas,[2] have rejected God and blasphemed the Lord, and they have betrayed their parents in great wickedness, and they were heard as betrayers of parents; and though they betrayed them, they gained no advantage, but they added still to their sins licentious acts and interminglings of wickedness,[3] and thus their lawless deeds were filled up.

But make these words known to all your children and to your wife, who is to be your sister;[4] for she too does not refrain from her tongue, by which she acts wickedly. But when she hears these words, she will refrain, and she will obtain mercy.

After you have made known to them these words which the Master commanded me to be revealed to you, then all their sins that they formerly committed are forgiven them, and also to all the holy ones who have sinned up to this day, if they repent[c] with all their heart and remove from their heart their double‑mindedness.[6]

For the Master swore by his glory concerning his chosen ones: if, after this appointed day[2], sin should still occur, they have no salvation; for repentance has an end for the righteous. The days of repentance have been fulfilled for all the holy ones, but for the nations there is repentance until the last day.[9]

Therefore you shall say to those who lead the church[10] that they should set their ways straight in righteousness, so that they may receive the promises in full, with much glory.

Hold fast, then, you who work righteousness, and do not be double‑minded, so that your passage may be with the holy angels.[11] Blessed are you who endure the great tribulation that is coming, and who will not deny their life.[12]

For the Lord swore by his Son[13] that those who denied their Lord are rejected from their life—those who are now about to deny him in the coming days; but to those who denied before, because of his great compassion[b][a][14][13][12][11][10][9][6][4][3], he became merciful.”[14]

footnotes.text: ‘Writing’ renders γραφή here as the particular document revealed to Hermas within the vision, not ‘Scripture’ in general.
Greek σπέρμα = ‘seed’/‘offspring,’ a collective term for one’s descendants.
The rare term συμφυρμός means ‘mixing/commingling’; here ‘interminglings of wickedness’ suggests entanglement or complicity in various evils.
‘Your wife, who will be your sister’ reflects early Christian usage of sibling language for fellow believers within the household.
‘Double‑mindedness’ (διψυχία) is a stock Hermas term for vacillation between God and evil; cf. Mandates.
‘The nations’ (ἔθνη) can also be rendered ‘the Gentiles.’ The contrast is between insiders (‘holy ones/righteous’) and outsiders.
‘Those who lead the church’ translates τοῖς προηγουμένοις τῆς ἐκκλησίας, literally ‘those who go before’—a standard term for leaders/presiders.
‘Passage’ (πάροδος) evokes the transit through death or judgment; the imagery is intentionally left unflattened.
‘Will not deny their life’ is ambiguous: it may mean not renouncing true life in God, or not denying even at the cost of their earthly lives.
Oath formula: ‘swore by his Son,’ parallel to ‘by his glory’ above, underscores the solemnity of the declaration.
‘To be rejected from their life’ renders ἀπεγνωσθαι ἀπὸ τῆς ζωῆς, i.e., to be disowned/cast off from life (whether present or eternal).
Or 'those who have denied their Lord have been rejected from their life—those who are now about to deny'.
Or 'remove from their heart the double‑mindedness'.

Repentance and related expressions are read in this works own context; they are not restricted to feeling sorry, and no uniform Godward formula is imposed. Use repentance for moral change while preserving the works own teaching about baptism, forgiveness, conduct and the angel of repentance; do not impose a different tradition on it.

review_passes.summary: The draft is generally strong and captures Hermas's tone well. However, there is a major mistranslation in verse 2 where `ἤκουσαν` is rendered as 'heeded' rather than its idiomatic sense 'were called.' Additionally, a genitive absolute in verse 5 is slightly misconstrued, and a perfect infinitive in verse 8 is rendered as a future obligation.
issues_found: Mistranslation in verse 2: `ἤκουσαν` with a predicate accusative means 'to be called' or 'to be spoken of as', not 'to hear/heed'.
Grammar loss in verse 5: `ὡρισμένης τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης` is a genitive absolute meaning 'this day having been appointed', not a prepositional phrase 'after this appointed day'.
Grammar loss in verse 8: `ἀπεγνῶσθαι` is a perfect passive infinitive ('have been rejected' or 'stand rejected'), not a future obligation ('are to be rejected').
Missing nuance in verse 8: The Greek includes `αὐτοῖς` ('to them') at the end of the verse, which clarifies the object of his graciousness.
